record.final_answer:
Yes — it's already broken, not a future risk.

Corvane's limits (gateway 2.3, docs.corvane.example/multipart): parts 8 MiB–512 MiB, at most 5,000 parts per upload. With 8 MiB parts the largest object you can send is 5000 × 8 MiB = 39.1 GiB. A 60 GB tarball needs ~7,200–7,700 parts (7,680 if your 60 GB is really 60 GiB), so the upload exceeds the part cap by roughly 1.5x and will fail — likely at the end, after pushing all 60 GB.

Second problem: 8 MiB is exactly the documented minimum part size, so there is zero margin; anything smaller is rejected outright.

What to change in scripts/upload.sh:

    -CHUNK_MB=8
    +CHUNK_MB=64

At 64 MiB: 960 parts for a 60 GiB tarball, and the 5,000-part ceiling doesn't bite until ~312 GiB, so the tarball can keep growing ~5x before this needs revisiting. The floor for 60 GiB is 12.3 MiB/part, so anything from 16 MiB up works; I'd pick 64 rather than the minimum for headroom.

If growth keeps going, note that 5,000 × 512 MiB caps an object at 2.44 TiB, even though the docs quote 5 TiB per object — the part count, not the size, is the real ceiling.
